report_name: Exposed AWS Key Leads to Beacon CRM Data Breach Affecting Over 1,500 UK Charities

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Threat Actor
threat_actors.description: The threat actors who discovered and exploited an exposed AWS access key within public-facing JavaScript files to breach Beacon CRM's cloud environment.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the Beacon CRM platform, a software provider for the non-profit sector, leading to a downstream data breach for its 1,500+ client charities.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: A highly sensitive AWS access key was inadvertently exposed, hardcoded within a publicly accessible JavaScript build artifact.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: Attackers stole an AWS access key, which functions as an application access token, that was exposed in public code.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors used the stolen but legitimate AWS access key to authenticate to Beacon's AWS environment and gain unauthorized access.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access to the AWS environment, the attackers accessed client data, which was likely stored in cloud storage services such as S3 buckets.

identities.name: Beacon
identities.description: A customer relationship management (CRM) provider for the non-profit sector whose AWS environment was compromised due to an exposed access key, leading to a supply chain data breach for its clients.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services
identities.description: The cloud service provider whose access key was compromised. AWS itself was not breached, but its services were accessed illegitimately via the stolen credential.

identities.name: Over 1,500 UK Charities
identities.description: The downstream victims of the Beacon CRM supply chain attack, whose sensitive donor and operational data was potentially exposed.

indicators.name: Potential AWS Access Key Exposure
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential AWS Access Key Exposure in Code or Logs
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects patterns resembling AWS Access Key IDs in logs or files. This can indicate hardcoded credentials.
references:
  - https://securemonk.io/news/2026-08-14-am
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-15
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: all
detection:
  selection:
    keywords|re:
      - '(A3T[A-Z0-9]|AKIA|AGPA|AROA|ASCA)[A-Z0-9]{16}'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a regular expression pattern for AWS access key IDs, which could indicate credential exposure in code, configuration files, or logs.

indicators.name: Potential Hardcoded Secrets in Web Files
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Hardcoded Secret Keywords in Web Content
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-1b0a-9e8f7d6c5b4a
status: experimental
description: Detects keywords often associated with hardcoded secrets within public-facing JavaScript or JSON files.
references:
  - https://securemonk.io/news/2026-08-14-am
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-15
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains:
      - 'client_secret='
      - 'api_key='
      - '"client_secret":'
      - '"api_key":'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects keywords such as 'client_secret' and 'api_key' in web traffic, which could indicate secrets exposed in client-side files.

relationships.source_name: Potential Hardcoded Secrets in Web Files
